clue.text: What's highly desirable bachelor hairstyle? Something hanging straight down

parts.note: a plum job or role is a highly desirable one
B is the standard abbreviation for bachelor, as in a degree
a bob is a short haircut level with the jaw

explanation.surface: A question about what haircut a sought-after single man would favour.
explanation.definitionFit: A weight on a line used by builders to find the true vertical hangs straight down.

clue.text: Depart, split, head off

indicators.note: head off says the first letter of the word for split is removed

parts.note: to cleave is to split, as with an axe

explanation.surface: Three terse instructions for clearing out fast, as if fleeing.
explanation.definitionFit: To go away from a place is a plain synonym of depart.

clue.text: Compelled to request meal in restaurant a la carte

parts.note: made someone do something means compelled them
taken as written
to order is to ask a waiter for food

explanation.surface: A diner is forced to choose a dish from the menu rather than a set meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishes chosen separately from a menu are cooked individually on demand, made to a customer's request.

clue.text: Type of shares he distributed with public

indicators.note: distributed suggests the letters are spread around and redealt in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone hands out stock to ordinary members of the public.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock in large, reliable, well-established companies is called by this poker-derived name.

clue.text: Somehow definitely close to pirate gold, according to thief

parts.note: by means near or beside, as in 'stand by the door'
Captain Hook is the pirate in Peter Pan
or is the heraldic word for gold
by can mean according to, as in 'by the rules'
a crook is a criminal such as a thief

explanation.surface: A tale of a pirate's treasure, told the way a thief would see it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means by any means necessary, so something will certainly happen one way or another.

clue.text: Scottish general pronouncement of trouble for financial house?

indicators.note: pronouncement says the phrase is to be spoken and heard rather than spelt

parts.note: woe for a bank, read as a two-word phrase

explanation.surface: A soldier from Scotland announces bad news for a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: Bank woe, said out loud, gives the name of the general murdered in Shakespeare's Macbeth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Macbeth this character is a Scottish general and Macbeth's fellow commander.

clue.text: Sibling loses early resistance to worry

indicators.note: loses early says the letter is dropped from near the front of the word

parts.note: a brother is a male sibling
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A brother gives up his early opposition to fretting.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouble or annoy someone is a common synonym of worry.

clue.text: Neither chap was up

indicators.note: in a down entry, was up says the name is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Ron is a man's name, a chap in crossword terms

explanation.surface: A remark that no man had got out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction pairs with neither in negative lists, so it stands as its partner word.

clue.text: Showing embarrassment after UN fellow is exposed

indicators.note: after places the word for blushing behind the other pieces

parts.note: the United Nations, taken as written
cove is old British slang for a man or fellow
someone embarrassed goes red in the face

explanation.surface: A man at the United Nations blushes after his secret comes out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncovered has had its covering removed, so it lies open and exposed.

clue.text: State gold carriage

parts.note: a land is a country or state
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A gilded coach used on ceremonial state occasions.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle with a folding hood is a kind of carriage.

clue.text: Horse races beset by a sprain but wins on the trot

parts.note: H is slang for heroin, known as horse

indicators.note: beset by says the races are surrounded by the following pieces

parts.note: a rick is a sprain or wrench
the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorbike races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A horse hampered by an injury still wins race after race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the trot' is British for in succession, and 'Horse' is slang for heroin, not an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Three successive wins or goals by the same player or team form this feat.

clue.text: Famous scientist gives up on amphibian

indicators.note: gives up says the word on is surrendered from the end of the scientist's name

parts.note: Isaac Newton, the physicist of gravity fame

explanation.surface: A great scientist abandons his work on frogs and their kin.
explanation.definitionFit: A small salamander-like creature that lives partly in water is an example of an amphibian.

clue.text: Narrow escape — wastes hour in pothole

indicators.note: in places the wasting and the hour inside the underground hollow

parts.note: a pothole is a deep natural cave
to lose time is to waste it

explanation.surface: A caver squanders an hour underground and barely gets out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase, from a razor nearly cutting skin, means a near miss or narrow escape.

clue.text: Humane moves to secure changes in cruel Italian town

indicators.note: to secure says the first scramble holds the second inside it
moves says the letters of the first word are shifted about
changes in says the letters of the second word are altered in order

explanation.surface: A kindly reform aims to protect animals from cruel treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humane' tempts as a description of the reform, but it is anagram fodder; 'moves' and 'changes in' each signal a separate rearrangement, and the second scramble sits inside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: This Roman town near Naples was buried by Vesuvius in AD 79, an Italian town.

clue.text: Battle of 1812's composer with overture's beginning

parts.note: Alexander Borodin was a Russian composer

indicators.note: beginning says only the opening letter of overture is used

explanation.surface: Tchaikovsky's 1812 Overture celebrates a battle; here a different composer joins it.
explanation.definitionFit: The bloody clash outside Moscow in 1812 between Napoleon and the Russians bears this name.

clue.text: Being unaware left one in clear

indicators.note: in places left and one inside the word for clear

parts.note: something obvious is clear
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone who has no idea is left out in the open.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not noticing what is going on around them is described this way.

clue.text: Very unusual rupees exist

parts.note: things that are, exist

explanation.surface: A remark that rupees really are hard to find.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seldom found or occurring is very unusual.

clue.text: Sliced vegetables appeal, served in natural oils

indicators.note: served in says appeal is placed inside the oils

parts.note: crudes are unrefined petroleum oils
it is sex appeal, as in 'she's got it'

explanation.surface: Vegetables dressed in good oils make an appealing starter.
explanation.definitionFit: This French starter consists of raw vegetables cut into strips, served with dips.

clue.text: Pleased with good boy

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A parent is happy with a well-behaved son.
explanation.definitionFit: Being happy about something is a plain synonym of pleased.

clue.text: One French drink you initially wanted after food is knocked back?

definitions.text: One French drink you initially wanted after food is knocked back?

indicators.note: after places the French one and the initials behind the reversed food
knocked back says the word for food is turned round

parts.note: grub is slang for food
un is French for one

indicators.note: initially says the first letters of drink and you are used

explanation.surface: After downing a meal you naturally want a French wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' turns the food word round to BURG. The whole clue describes a wine served with or after food, so it defines too.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine from the Burgundy region of France is a French drink often enjoyed with a meal.

clue.text: Wander randomly? Not entirely purposeful journey

indicators.note: not entirely says the answer is part of the words, not the whole of them

explanation.surface: A question about aimless wandering, set against a trip with a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wander' tempts as the definition, but the trip is purposeful, not random.
explanation.definitionFit: A short trip made to do a particular task, like shopping, is a purposeful journey.

clue.text: Caught Verdi opera: shortened, badly produced, and too expensive

indicators.note: badly produced says the pieces are put together in a jumbled order

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: shortened says the last letter of opera is cut off

explanation.surface: A review of a cut and poorly staged Verdi production that cost too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' turns OPERA into OPER; C, VERDI and OPER are then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something priced higher than it is worth costs too much, so it is too expensive.

clue.text: Mediterranean port area

definitions.meaning: a historic harbour city in northern Israel on the Mediterranean coast
a unit of land area, 4840 square yards

explanation.surface: A Mediterranean harbour and its land.
explanation.definitionFit: The port in Israel and the imperial unit of land measure share this name.

clue.text: Tees, perhaps, golf club's beheaded

indicators.note: beheaded says the club loses its first letter

parts.note: a driver is a golf club used off the tee

explanation.surface: A golfer's club loses its head on the tee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tees' looks like golf tees, but it is the river in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tees is a river in north-east England, given as an example.

clue.text: State of Oregon having trouble after California has change 'of heart

indicators.note: after places Oregon and trouble behind the altered abbreviation
change of heart says the middle letter of the abbreviation is swapped for another

parts.note: OR is the postal abbreviation for Oregon
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: Oregon's troubles follow California changing its mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has change of heart' swaps the A in the middle of CAL for O, giving COL.
explanation.definitionFit: This mountain state of the western USA is one of the fifty states.

clue.text: Recited outstanding poem

indicators.note: recited says the word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a debt still owed is outstanding; the letters running backwards across the first two words are a coincidence

explanation.surface: Someone reads aloud a remarkable piece of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyric poem addressed to a subject in an elevated style is a kind of poem.

clue.text: Time we have to hold start of lunch?

definitions.text: Time we have to hold start of lunch?

indicators.note: to hold says the contracted words contain the next piece

parts.note: we have contracts to we've

indicators.note: start of says only the first letter of lunch is used

explanation.surface: Asking whether it is time for us to break for lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: noon, when lunch traditionally starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday, the number on the clock when lunch is often taken, is the time described.

clue.text: Like Conservative, aim to rise in status

parts.note: as means like
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A Tory politician aims to climb the social ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb or go up is to rise, here in rank or status.

clue.text: I'm rakish broken-down person in divided state

indicators.note: broken-down says the letters are smashed apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: A dissolute rogue confesses he is a wreck.
explanation.definitionFit: Kashmir is split between India and Pakistan, so a native of it comes from a divided state.
